Subject: Dedicated commit: tokens/sec & latency guarantees — initial ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting internal discussions about a reserved GPU commit and need to align on acceptance criteria for throughput guarantees. A few concrete questions to start:

- For a 50k tokens/sec committed pool (mixed chat + single-turn generation), how do you define the measurement window for the guarantee (sample window length, warm/cold cache treatment)?
- Do you expose both tokens/sec and requests/sec guarantees? If so, which one drives billing and which one is used for SLA credits?
- What's Redwood's standard approach for latency SLOs (p50/p95) in these acceptance runs? We expect p95 < 400ms for single-turn 128-token requests; can you confirm how you measure that?
- On discounts: we're proposing a 12-month commit. How are discount bands adjusted if observed throughput conformance is within X% of the committed rate?

Can you share a short test plan or checklist we can forward to our infra team? Also looping procurement on next steps.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Platform — Acme Dataworks

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. Summary and next steps below. Attaching our latest test plan and a GPU-sizer worksheet so you can model commit bands.

Quick answers up front:
- Measurement window: default acceptance window is 30 minutes sampled across 3 non-overlapping windows (3 x 30m samples) during business hours. We report both average tokens/sec and 95th-percentile of tokens/sec across samples. Cold-cache runs (first requests after restart) are excluded from primary acceptance; we strobe a warm-up period of 15 minutes before each sample.
- Metrics exposed: we provide tokens/sec (primary billing driver) and requests/sec (observability and fallback routing). SLA credits are calculated off the tokens/sec shortfall aggregated over the acceptance windows.
- Latency SLOs: we measure per-request latency and report p50/p95/p99 for the sampled requests in the acceptance windows. For single-turn 128-token requests we use the p95 over the sampled windows.
- Discounts and adjustment: our baseline proposal ties discount tiers to committed tokens/sec bands. If delivered throughput is within -5% of committed rate we consider the commit satisfied. For shortfalls >5%, crediting applies and we pro-rate discounts on a quarterly reconciliation. We can make explicit exceptions in the contract for force-majeure or workload profile mismatches.

Attached: dedicated_throughput_testplan_v3.pdf (test cases + pass/fail), gpu-pool-sizing-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-commit-proposal-ACME-2027.pdf

I'll schedule a short call with our SE (Laura) to walk the acceptance script and discuss warm cache / KV caching caveats. What times look good for you this week?

Cheers,

Hi Sanjay — Laura here (SE). I pulled the test plan into the Drive link Ben shared and sketched a couple of benchmark scenarios based on your 70/30 workload. Key points:

- Mixed-profile simulation: we can run a param-driven harness that replays your traffic mix (we'll need a sample trace or a short recording of recent requests). The acceptance harness supports per-session KV cache semantics so we can choose warm vs cold cache modes.
- Cache treatment: for contractual acceptance we run two passes:
  1) Warm-cache pass (default): 15m warm-up, then measurement windows. This reflects steady-state production performance and maps to billing.
  2) Cold-cache diagnostic pass: single short run with instrumentation to show worst-case cold-start latencies — not used for billing but included in the acceptance packet.
- Window sizing: we are flexible. For enterprise deals we commonly accept 4 x 1h windows when customers prefer longer variance smoothing. The acceptance report will include per-window tokens/sec, per-request latencies (p50/p95), and a combined compliance flag.

Operational notes:
- We'll request a temporary inbound test whitelist for the harness IPs and a short service account with metrics read ACLs.
- Our measurement tooling records both server-side timing and end-to-end client timing; we prefer server-side as the authoritative source for SLA credits.

Next steps: if you can share a 30–60 minute trace (redacted is fine) and confirm preferred windows (4x1h or 3x30m), I'll author an acceptance run schedule and share expected timings.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all — legal here. Two commercial points to confirm before we sign:

1) Credits & reconciliation cadence: if Redwood credits based on shortfall, we need clear quarterly reconciliation and a cap on annual credits (we usually ask for a 50% cap of the quarterly commit value). Please confirm standard cap and whether exceptions for infra maintenance will be excluded.

2) Discount waterfall: we need the explicit mapping between committed tokens/sec bands and discount percentage (for example: 0.5–0.9x = Tier A discount X, 0.9–1.0x = Tier B discount Y). Please include definitions for measurement tolerance (-5% = acceptable) and the path for remediation (tuning period + retest).

If you can incorporate those two items into the redwood-commit-proposal-ACME-2027.pdf and circulate a revised doc, legal will fast-track a review.

Best,
